lines.text: What would you do if a huge leopard seal swam straight at you with its mouth wide open?
That is what happened to the photographer Paul Nicklen, in the freezing water of Antarctica, while he was working for National Geographic magazine in two thousand six.
The seal was a female, and he says her head was bigger than a grizzly bear's.
Then she did something he never expected. She took his camera into her mouth, and then his head.
And then she let go. She did not hurt him.
What came next made even less sense. Over the next four days, she started bringing him penguins.
Why would a top predator of the Antarctic try to feed a human?
That is the question for this whole video, and I will give you the honest answer at the end, including the part where nobody is sure.
But first you need to know what kind of animal this is, because what leopard seals normally do to penguins is not gentle.
